previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A 68-year-old male with a history of quadriplegia, tracheostomy, GJ tube, and ileostomy was admitted from his nursing home for lethargy and leukocytosis. He was found to have a urinary tract infection caused by Klebsiella pneumoniae, acute kidney injury likely due to dehydration, and hypernatremia. He was treated with IV meropenem and IV fluids, leading to improvement in infection markers and renal function. His supratherapeutic INR led to temporary discontinuation of warfarin. His stage IV sacral ulcer was monitored with no evidence of osteomyelitis, and wound care recommendations were implemented. Iron deficiency anemia was addressed with oral ferrous sulfate, and oral thrush was treated with nystatin and chlorhexidine. He was discharged to extended care to complete his antibiotic course with stable vital signs and resolved symptoms.

radiology_notes.text:
HISTORY:  Stroke, chronic UTI and pneumonia with tachycardia.

TECHNIQUE:  Semi-upright AP view of the chest.

COMPARISON:  ___.

FINDINGS:

Study is slightly limited due to patient positioning.  Tracheostomy tube is in
standard position.  Heart size is moderately enlarged.  The mediastinal
contours are unchanged.  Streaky patchy opacities in the lung bases likely
reflect atelectasis.  There is crowding of the bronchovascular structures
likely due to low lung volumes.  Trace blunting of the right costophrenic
angle may suggest the presence of a trace pleural effusion.  No left-sided
pleural effusion is identified, and there is no pneumothorax.  Multilevel
degenerative changes are seen within the thoracic spine, as well as within the
right glenohumeral joint.

IMPRESSION:

Limited exam due to patient rotation.  Streaky bibasilar airspace opacities
could reflect atelectasis.  Pneumonia cannot be completely excluded.  Possible
trace right pleural effusion.

INDICATION:  Patient with sepsis and abdominal pain.  Assess for source of
sepsis.

COMPARISONS:  CT abdomen and pelvis of ___ and sacrum/coccyx
radiographs of ___.

TECHNIQUE:  MDCT-acquired contiguous images through the abdomen and pelvis
were obtained with intravenous contrast at 5-mm slice thickness.  Coronally
and sagittally reformatted images are provided.

FINDINGS:

CT OF THE ABDOMEN:

Consolidative opacities are seen in imaged lung bases.  No pleural effusion is
seen.  The heart is slightly enlarged without pericardial effusion.  Coronary
artery and aortic valve calcifications are mild to moderate.

The liver enhances homogeneously.  Focal hypodensities, like cysts or
hamartomas within the liver, are unchanged.  For example, a 7-mm hypodensity
in segment VIII is unchanged (2:16).  Bilobed hypodensity in segment III
measures 1.1 x 0.7 cm is stable (2:24).  An additional 5-mm hypodensity in the
caudate lobe is also unchanged (2:27).  No suspicious hepatic lesion is
identified.  There is no intrahepatic biliary ductal dilatation.  The
gallbladder is surgically absent.  Multiple surgical clips are seen within the
gallbladder fossa.  Spleen is unremarkable.  The pancreas is atrophic;
however, no pancreatic ductal dilatation or peripancreatic fluid collection is
seen.  The adrenal glands appear normal.  The kidneys enhance and excrete
contrast symmetrically without hydronephrosis.  Multiple renal hypodense
lesions are noted, which are essentially unchanged in size and distribution
since ___ exam.  The largest hypodense lesion in the interpolar region
of the right kidney measures 1.8 x 2.2 cm and 15 Hounsfield units in
attenuation (2:39).  Many of the renal hypodensities are too small to
characterize and most likely represent cysts.

A percutaneous gastrojejunostomy tube is in place, which appears appropriately
positioned.  There is no bowel obstruction.  Small bowel loops closely abut
the abdominal wall and appear unchanged in position since prior exam.  There
is no bowel wall thickening.  The patient is status post total colectomy.  The
ileostomy site in the right lower abdomen is unremarkable in appearance. 
Contrast material is seen traversing the distal ileal loops and exiting at the
ileostomy site.

There is no free air or free fluid within the abdomen. The intra-abdominal
aorta is notable for extensive calcified atherosclerotic disease without
associated aneurysmal changes.  There is no mesenteric or retroperitoneal
lymphadenopathy.

CT OF THE PELVIS:

A Foley catheter is in place.  The bladder is collapsed around the Foley
catheter with circumferential bladder wall thickening noted.  Perivesicular
fat stranding seen on prior exam is slightly improved. Small locules of gas
within the bladder (2:81) may relate to Foley placement or chronic underlying
infection.  There is no free air or free fluid within the pelvis.  There is no
pelvic lymphadenopathy.  The rectum is unremarkable.  The suture chain
involving the distal sigmoid colon is noted.

OSSEOUS STRUCTURES:  The bones are diffusely demineralized.  Post-surgical
changes related to right total hip arthroplasty are unchanged.  There is a
deep soft tissue ulcer involving the right gluteal region extending into the
right ischium.  There is associated fat stranding.  No definite osteolysis is
seen, however, the above findings are concerning for osteomyelitis.

IMPRESSION:

1.  Bilateral lower lobe consolidation, concerning for pneumonia or
aspiration.

2.  Deep soft tissue ulcer involving the right gluteal region extending into
the right ischium, raising concern for underlying osteomyelitis.

3.  Multiple hepatic hypodensities, likely cysts or hamartomas are unchanged
since ___ exam.

4. Multiple renal hypodense lesions, many of which are too small to
characterize, are unchanged in size and distribution since ___ study.

5.  Bladder wall thickening may reflect cystitis which appears chronic, but
improved.

SINGLE FRONTAL VIEW OF THE CHEST.

REASON FOR EXAM:  Assess line.

Comparison is made with prior study ___.

Right PICC tip is in the lower SVC.  Tracheostomy tube is place.  Opacities in
the left lower lobe have increased consistent with increase in small left
pleural effusion and adjacent atelectasis.  There are low lung volumes.  The
aorta is tortuous.  Mild cardiomegaly is stable.  If any, there is small right
pleural effusion.  Right lower lobe atelectasis is unchanged.  There is mild
vascular congestion.

HISTORY:  ___ with history of stoke and quadriplegia at baseline,
presenting with fevers and decubitus ulcer.  Evaluation for ischial
osteomyelitis.

TECHNIQUE:  Multi sequence, multiplanar MRI of the pelvis was obtained without
and following administration of IV contrast, on 1.5 tesla magnet.

COMPARISON:  CT of the pelvis from ___.


FINDINGS:  

There is a large decubitus ulcer involving the right buttocks, with extension
of ulceration to the adjacent right ischial tuberosity.  There is diffuse
inflammation involving the ulcer and right ischial tuberosity.  Notable amount
of edema involving the ischial tuberosity with associated enhancement -- fiven
the presence of overlying ulcer, this is consistent with osteomyelitis.  There
is trace amount of edema also tracking along the attachment of the hamstrings
on the ischial tuberosity without definite tear of the tendon seen.

No evidence of abscess.

There is significant amount of hardware artifact emanating from the right
femur, from prior arthroplasty, limiting adequate evaluation for joint
effusion or other joint pathology.  Allowing for this limitation, no gross
joint effusion seen.  

The rest of the visualized bones including the sacrum appears unremarkable.

There are multiple enlarged reactive lymph nodes in the right groin, likely
reactive.

The contralateral left hip and ischial tuberosity are within normal limits.

The urinary bladder is decompressed with Foley catheter.  

There is mild diffuse atrophy involving all muscles surrounding the right hip,
likely secondary to disuse.


IMPRESSION:
1.  MRI findings highly suggestive of osteomyelitis within the right ischial
tuberosity.  
2.  Large ulcer involving the right buttock, with extension to the right
ischial tuberosity as described.  No evidence of abscess.  

NOTIFICATION:  These critical findings were discussed with Dr. ___
at 13:34 on ___ ___, phone).

REASON FOR EXAMINATION:  Evaluation of the patient after PICC line placement.

Portable AP radiograph of the chest was reviewed in comparison to ___.

The right PICC line tip is at the mid SVC level.  Heart size and mediastinal
are unchanged in appearance.  Bilateral left more than right pleural effusions
and bibasilar atelectasis are unchanged.  No new pneumothorax is seen. 
Tracheostomy is in place.
